primary_citation: 15 U.S.C. §1638 (Truth in Lending Act, Pub. L. 90-321 (1968); current version through Pub. L. 111-203, Dodd-Frank (2010))
short_title: Truth in Lending Act §1638 — Auto Financing Disclosure Requirements; Yo-Yo Financing Violations
one_line_rule: Creditors must disclose the APR, finance charge, payment schedule, and total of payments accurately before consummating closed-end credit (including auto financing); inaccurate or changed terms in yo-yo financing = TILA violation; civil remedy $100-$1,000 statutory minimum + actual damages + mandatory attorneys' fees.

case_law.cite: Ford Motor Credit Co. v. Milhollin, 444 U.S. 555 (1980)
case_law.court: Supreme Court of the United States
case_law.key_rule: Courts defer to Federal Reserve Board (now CFPB) Regulation Z interpretations; Official Staff Commentary is authoritative for specific disclosure requirements; APR is the central TILA disclosure; purpose of enabling comparison shopping informs all disclosure requirements. Note: deference aspect weakened by Loper Bright (2024).

case_law.cite: CFPB Auto Finance Examination Procedures + Supervisory Highlights (pattern 2011-present)
case_law.key_rule: Yo-yo financing with inaccurate APR = TILA violation; spot delivery where original terms don't match final terms = TILA violation; TILA affirmative defense available in collection actions without SOL; CFPB examines auto financing TILA compliance as priority area.
